name: Question 5
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054607/assets/a51b5dca6436e6ffd3af0d1cfa801141d97e7660e6218344011a5ac965c722c6.png)

If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y=2(x-2)^{2}-1$ and $y=2-(x-2)^{2},$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054607/assets/a15535c1eee33018c0486fd3cf1900fd151a9a23cf374c6a0ccec60ca47c64c3.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 3,\,2(x-2)^{2}-1\le y\le 2-(x-2)^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{2(x-2)^{2}-1}^{2-(x-2)^{2}}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[{\int }_{2(x-2)^{2}-1}^{2-(x-2)^{2}}f(x,y)\,dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

If D is the finite region enclosed by the curves y=2(x−2)2−1 and y=2−(x−2)2, as shown above, then ∬Df(x,y)dA=

a
∫13[∫2(x−2)2−12−(x−2)2f(x,y)dy]dx
b
∫13[∫2−(x−2)22(x−2)2−1f(x,y)dy]dx
c
∫13[∫2(x−2)2(x−2)2f(x,y)dy]dx
d
∫2(x−2)2−12−(x−2)2[∫13f(x,y)dy]dx
e
∫03[∫2x2−12+x2f(x,y)dy]dx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's represent D as a type I region. To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

As a result, we get

D={(x,y):1≤x≤3,2(x−2)2−1≤y≤2−(x−2)2}.

Therefore, we can express the integral, as follows:

∬Df(x,y)dA=∫13∫2(x−2)2−12−(x−2)2f(x,y)dydx=∫13[∫2(x−2)2−12−(x−2)2f(x,y)dy]dx
